report.summary: Reviewed chunk 5 of 5: cached_index and score_modules with single-flight lock and churn scoring.
risks: cached_index | medium | _build_lock uses key based on resolved root and scope; if key collision occurs between different scopes, builds may be serialized incorrectly. | Audit _build_lock implementation for key uniqueness.
cached_index | low | _INDEX_CACHE.pop(key, None) on refresh may remove a newly built entry from another thread if key matches exactly. | Verify that refresh and concurrent builds do not interfere.
score_modules | low | Division by zero if loc is 0; but modules with loc=0 are unlikely. | Ensure loc is always positive or handle zero gracefully.

handoff.purpose: Implements cached_index with single-flight pattern and score_modules for churn-aware complexity ranking.

symbols.name: cached_index
symbols.note: Process-wide index cache with single-flight lock; returns dict.

symbols.name: _hotspots
symbols.note: Returns top-N slice of score_modules result.

symbols.name: score_modules
symbols.note: Computes complexity-churn score for each module, returns sorted list.

claims.text: build_index is expensive on big repos; the first caller warms it and everyone (the web endpoints, the Ikarus chat brain) reuses it.
claims.why: build_index is not defined in this chunk; caching behavior is present but cannot verify cost or reuse by other components.

claims.text: SINGLE-FLIGHT (load-bearing): the cache is only populated *after* a build finishes, so without a per-root lock every concurrent caller saw a cold cache and started its OWN full scan.
claims.why: The code uses _build_lock(key) to serialize builds and checks cache under lock, preventing duplicate builds.

claims.text: The web server is a ThreadingHTTPServer, so switching panels mid-index spawned a second 6.8k-file scan instead of reusing the first -- each holding a complete index and its own tree-sitter parsers, which exhausted memory and took the page down.
claims.why: Reference to external server implementation and specific incident not present in this chunk.

claims.text: Concurrent callers now block on the in-flight build and share its result.
claims.why: The _build_lock context manager ensures only one build per key; subsequent callers wait and then return the cached result.

claims.text: The scope fingerprint is PART OF THE KEY: the cached index is a function of the center and the ignore rules as well as the root, so changing either must not hand back the index built under the old scope.
claims.why: key = _scope_key(resolved, scope, docs_on, types_on, wiki_on) includes scope derived from center and ignore.

claims.text: An unscoped repo keeps its bare path key, so nothing changes for repos that never configure this.
claims.why: project_scope is not defined here; cannot verify that unscoped repos return a bare path key.

claims.text: documents is resolved ONCE, here, and the same resolved boolean is used for both the key and the build.
claims.why: docs_on = documents_enabled(documents) is called once and passed to both key and build_index.

claims.text: Reading the env var independently in build_index would let the two disagree if it changed between the two reads, and the cache would then be keyed for one answer while holding the other.
claims.why: build_index is not in this chunk; cannot verify that it reads env var independently.

claims.text: types is resolved here for the same reason and with the same hazard: a key built from one reading of the env var and a build from another would cache a type-bearing index under the key for a type-free one.
claims.why: types_on = types_enabled(types) is called once and passed to key and build_index.

claims.text: wiki follows the identical discipline, and for the identical hazard: resolved ONCE here so the key and the build cannot disagree.
claims.why: wiki_on = wiki_enabled(wiki) and docs_on is computed once and used in key and build_index.

claims.text: It also depends on docs_on, so that conjunction is computed here too rather than being re-derived inside build_index where the key can no longer see it -- a key that said '+wiki' over a wiki-free index is exactly the silent-mismatch bug the documents flag already had to close.
claims.why: wiki_on is computed using docs_on here, and both are passed to key and build_index.

claims.text: Top-top slice of the full churn x complexity ranking.
claims.why: The function returns score_modules(modules, churn)[:top], which is a slice of the full ranking.

claims.text: Base score = long fns * 3 + guard_count + loc/50 (+ cc_max if present).
claims.why: base = len(m.get('long_functions', [])) * 3 + m.get('guard_count', 0) + m['loc'] / 50; then base += m.get('cc_max', 0).

claims.text: Final score = base * (1 + churn/max_churn). If churn is empty/None the factor is exactly 1.0 -> behaves identically to the pre-churn ranking (no regression); a churn field is added to every row regardless.
claims.why: score = base * (1 + churn_norm) where churn_norm = file_churn/max_churn if max_churn>0 else 0.0; churn field is added to each row.

claims.text: Returned whole rather than pre-trimmed so the code map can heat-shade every node from the same scoring pass that produces the hotspot list.
claims.why: The function returns the full scored list without trimming; _hotspots trims externally.

observations.what: cached_index uses a single-flight pattern with _build_lock to prevent concurrent builds for the same key.
score_modules computes a churn-weighted complexity score and returns all modules sorted by score.
The key includes resolved root, scope, and flags (docs_on, types_on, wiki_on); refresh pops the key from cache before rebuild.
score_modules assumes m['loc'] exists and is numeric; missing loc would cause KeyError.
The docstring for cached_index contains detailed narrative about past bugs and design rationale, but some claims reference code not present in this chunk (e.g., build_index, project_scope).
